content.text:
Done. Here's what changed and why each decision was made:

**`HeapHelper` is now `private static class HeapHelper<T extends Comparable<T>>`** inside `MinHeap`. `static` is correct here because the nested class carries its own `<T>` type parameter and holds its own reference to the list — it doesn't need an implicit reference to the outer `MinHeap` instance. Making it `private` means no other class in the package can see or instantiate it.

**`left` and `right` helpers inlined into `siftDown`** — they were already private and only called in one place inside `HeapHelper`, so keeping them as named methods added no clarity. `parent` stays as a named method because `MinHeap.delete` calls `helper.parent(index)` to decide the sift direction.

**`heapArray` encapsulation is unchanged but now fully enforced** — it was already `private final` in `MinHeap`, and the only thing that ever held a reference to it (`HeapHelper`) is now also private and nested, so no external code path can reach the list at all.

**`HeapHelper.java` deleted** — the type exists solely to serve `MinHeap`; a separate file would expose it at package scope.
